sections.label: Forward Singapore social compact
sections.summary: The Forward Singapore exercise brings Singaporeans together to refresh the social compact, with the Strategy Group developing new policy responses.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We see fraying social compacts in many countries around the world, where people feel excluded from their nation’s progress and cannot find a common way forward on important national issues.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is why we are embarking on the Forward Singapore exercise – to bring Singaporeans together to examine our shared values and responsibilities towards one another, and to refresh our social compact.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Strategy Group will work with Government agencies to refresh our strategies and develop new policy responses, so that Singaporeans will have opportunities to progress throughout life, stronger assurances to tide over difficult times and a renewed sense of solidarity for the future.

sections.label: Fertility and ageing population
sections.summary: Singapore faces a declining total fertility rate and an ageing population, like other advanced economies.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Like other advanced economies, Singapore faces a declining total fertility rate and an ageing population.

sections.label: Foreign worker and family support
sections.summary: The Government will manage foreign worker and immigration flows and strengthen support for families.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Second, the Government will continue to carefully manage our foreign worker and immigration flows, to ensure that these translate to tangible benefits for Singaporeans, and to help newcomers integrate better into our society.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Third, we will strengthen efforts to build a society where families matter and are well supported.

sections.label: Climate target and carbon tax
sections.summary: Singapore raised its climate target and plans to raise the carbon tax to $50 to $80 per tonne by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Last year, Singapore raised our national climate target – to reduce our emissions to around 60 million tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent in 2030, after peaking our emissions earlier, and to get to net-zero emissions by 2050.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: To achieve these targets, the Government plans to raise the carbon tax to a range of $50 to $80 per tonne of carbon dioxide equivalent by 2030.

sections.label: Preparing for global warming
sections.summary: The Strategy Group is working with Government agencies to prepare Singapore for global warming effects such as rising sea levels.

sentences.speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The Strategy Group is concurrently working with Government agencies to prepare Singapore for the effects of global warming, such as rising sea levels and temperatures, and the increasing frequency of extreme weather events.
